subject: Clarifying hosting constraints and next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@helixhealth.com>, security@helixhealth.com
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying hosting constraints and next steps

Hi Priya / Helix security team —

Thanks again for the time on the call today. Quick recap and a short list of clarifying questions so we can confirm whether Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, or a Private deployment is the right fit for your compliance requirements. I’ve attached a short checklist and two reference docs for the items below.

Recap (brief):
- Primary drivers: customer-managed key control (BYOK/HSM), 7-year log retention for audit, IdP-driven SSO + SCIM provisioning, and formal data residency to us-east-1.
- Procurement target: end of Q2 for an initial pilot (POC).

Questions (please answer inline if possible):
1) SSO / identity: Do you require SAML 2.0 + SCIM for automated user provisioning? Any specific IdP metadata we should expect?
2) KMS / HSM: Is the requirement strict customer-managed keys (no Redwood access), or is a cloud-KMS with customer CMK import acceptable? Do you have an HSM vendor preference?
3) Logging & retention: Confirm 7-year retention for audit logs. Do logs need to live in your AWS account (S3) or streamed to your Splunk instance? Any retention tiers (hot/warm/cold) we should model?
4) Network & deployment: If we provision Dedicated capacity, would VPC peering be acceptable, or do you need an on-prem / air-gapped Private deployment?

Proposed next steps:
- If you can confirm 1–4 above, Alex (SE) and I will prepare a short technical note mapping each requirement to Hosted / Dedicated / Private options and the expected timeline/risks.
- Schedule a technical deep dive with your infra and infosec (Alex suggested Thurs or Fri next week).

Attachments: redwood-private-deployment-checklist.docx, redwood-kms-hsm-integration.pdf, redwood-logging-retention-matrix.csv (attached for reference).

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@helixhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: security@helixhealth.com
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying hosting constraints and next steps

Rachel —

Appreciate the recap. Answers below inline.

> 1) SSO / identity: Do you require SAML 2.0 + SCIM for automated user provisioning? Any specific IdP metadata we should expect?
We require SAML 2.0 SSO (IdP-initiated + SP-initiated flows) and SCIM for provisioning and de-provisioning. Our IdP is Okta; we can share metadata files. SCIM should support groups and role syncing (we map roles to RBAC in our apps).

> 2) KMS / HSM: Is the requirement strict customer-managed keys (no Redwood access), or is a cloud-KMS with customer CMK import acceptable? Do you have an HSM vendor preference?
For production, Helix requires customer-managed keys with no vendor access. We prefer keys to live in our AWS account (KMS CMKs) or in an HSM appliance we control. If Redwood can support a KMS proxy or HSM integration that allows us to keep key material, that would be acceptable.

> 3) Logging & retention: Confirm 7-year retention for audit logs. Do logs need to live in your AWS account (S3) or streamed to your Splunk instance? Any retention tiers (hot/warm/cold) we should model?
Yes — 7 years for audit/security logs. Preferred is that logs are exported to our S3 bucket (us-east-1) and also forwarded to our Splunk instance for near-real-time monitoring. We can discuss retention lifecycle (hot -> cold) but the primary must be exportable and immutable for at least 7 years.

> 4) Network & deployment: If we provision Dedicated capacity, would VPC peering be acceptable, or do you need an on-prem / air-gapped Private deployment?
Dedicated with VPC peering would be fine for a pilot, but for full production we'll likely require a Private deployment (customer VPC or on-prem VM/HSM) depending on the key access guarantees. Procurement target remains end of Q2.

Can we schedule a 45-minute technical call Thurs 25th at 10am PT with our cloud infra and infosec? If Alex and Marissa can join that'd be great. I'll circulate an updated NDA and a short security questionnaire ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Priya Desai
Head of Cloud Security, Helix Health
priya.desai@helixhealth.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@helixhealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 07:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying hosting constraints and next steps

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear answers. Quick technical summary and how each hosting option maps to your requirements (high level):

SSO / SCIM:
- We fully support SAML 2.0 and SCIM v2. Okta is a common IdP for customers; we can consume Okta metadata and push role/group mappings into Redwood RBAC.

KMS / HSM:
- Hosted API: not suitable for customer-held raw key material — but we can support envelope encryption where you hold a master CMK in your AWS account and we use a short-lived data key workflow (requires KMS grant patterns).
- Dedicated: supports customer KMS in cloud via a KMS proxy or customer CMK import depending on cloud provider; operator access is limited and key operations can be proxied through your account.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full support for bringing your KMS/HSM (we can integrate with AWS KMS in your account or an on-prem HSM via PKCS#11). This is the only path that guarantees no Redwood access to key material in practice.

Logging & retention:
- We can stream audit logs to your Splunk (HTTPS/HEC) and/or push to an S3 bucket in your account (us-east-1). Logs can be written as append-only objects and lifecycle rules applied in your S3 for hot/cold tiers.
- For Dedicated and Private, we support configurable retention up to multi-year and can provide signed, immutable log exports for compliance.

Attachments included (short):
- redwood-kms-hsm-integration.pdf — technical notes on KMS proxy and PKCS#11 integration.
- redwood-logging-retention-matrix.csv — suggested retention profiles and S3 lifecycle examples.
- redwood-private-deployment-checklist.docx — network/VPC and procurement checklist for Private deployments.

Risks / notes:
- Hosted API will not meet the strict Helix requirement for zero vendor access to key material; recommend Dedicated pilot to validate performance + SSO/SCIM integration, with Private deployment scoped for production if Helix requires absolute key custody.
- Time for Private onboarding (if on-prem HSM required) typically 6–12 weeks after contract signature depending on access scheduling and HSM provisioning.

Next step: Please confirm the Thurs 25th 10am PT slot for a 45-minute technical call and list attendees (cloud infra + infosec). We'll prepare a short demo of the KMS proxy flow and a logging export example.

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
